games.title: Vampire: The Masquerade
games.note: Mark Rein-Hagen's tabletop game of vampire clans hiding from humanity in a 'gothic-punk' modern world.

games.title: Numenera
games.note: Monte Cook's science-fantasy RPG set in the Ninth World, about a billion years in the future.

games.title: Shadowrun
games.note: FASA's tabletop RPG mixing a cyberpunk future with returning magic, elves and dragons.

games.title: Shadowrun Returns
games.note: Shadowrun co-creator Jordan Weisman funded it on Kickstarter in 2012; it shipped with an editor for player-made campaigns.

games.title: Wasteland 2
games.note: Crowdfunded on Kickstarter, with original designers Alan Pavlish, Michael Stackpole, Ken St. Andre and Liz Danforth on the team.

games.title: Wasteland 3
games.note: Moves the Desert Rangers from Arizona to snowbound Colorado.

games.title: Planescape: Torment
games.note: You play an immortal who has forgotten his past lives; lead designer Chris Avellone put talking ahead of fighting.

games.title: Icewind Dale
games.note: A combat-heavy Infinity Engine dungeon crawl set in the frozen north of the Forgotten Realms.

games.title: Neverwinter Nights
games.note: Shipped with the Aurora toolset, so players could build their own modules and run them online as Dungeon Masters.

games.title: Neverwinter Nights 2
games.note: Obsidian's sequel to BioWare's game, using D&D 3.5 rules and an updated toolset.

games.title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
games.note: Set thousands of years before the films so BioWare could invent freely; its rules come from a D&D-based Star Wars tabletop game.

games.title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords
games.note: LucasArts gave Obsidian only 14 to 16 months, so it shipped with cut content that fans later restored.

games.title: Jade Empire
games.note: BioWare's first original RPG world, drawing on Chinese mythology, wuxia films and Journey to the West.

games.title: Pillars of Eternity
games.note: Directed by Josh Sawyer; its 2012 Kickstarter, pitched as 'Project Eternity', passed $1.4 million in three days.

games.title: Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire
games.note: Trades the first game's stronghold for a ship sailing between the islands of the Deadfire Archipelago.

games.title: Tyranny
games.note: You serve an overlord whose armies of evil have already won the war.

games.title: Torment: Tides of Numenera
games.note: Its 2013 Kickstarter hit its $900,000 goal within hours and went on to pass $4 million.

games.title: Pentiment
games.note: A murder mystery in 16th-century Bavaria, drawn in the style of illuminated manuscripts.

games.title: Avowed
games.note: A first-person action RPG set in Eora, the world of Pillars of Eternity, directed by Carrie Patel; released February 2025.

games.title: Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines
games.note: Valve's contract barred it from launching before Half-Life 2, so the two Source engine games arrived together in November 2004.

games.title: Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines 2
games.note: Begun by Hardsuit Labs and finished by The Chinese Room, it came out 21 years after the original.

games.title: Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura
games.note: Troika's first game: a fantasy world in the middle of an industrial revolution, where magic and machines clash.

games.title: The Temple of Elemental Evil
games.note: Adapts Gary Gygax's 1985 adventure module and was the first computer game to use the D&D 3.5 rules.

games.title: Mass Effect: Andromeda
games.note: Sends colonists on a 600-year journey to the Andromeda galaxy, away from the original trilogy's events.

games.title: Dragon Age: The Veilguard
games.note: Released ten years after Inquisition; it was first announced under the name Dreadwolf.

links.took: A post-nuclear setting, open-ended quests and more than one way to solve problems.
links.added: Turn-based combat, the SPECIAL character system, dark humor and 1950s retro-future style.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fallout (Interplay called it Wasteland's spiritual successor)

links.extra: EA owned the Wasteland name, so Interplay could not make a direct sequel. Almost everyone on the team had played Wasteland.

links.took: Its first rules: Fallout was built on GURPS until early 1997.
links.added: Its own SPECIAL system, made in a hurry after Steve Jackson Games objected to the violence.
links.extra: Christopher Taylor designed SPECIAL and Tim Cain coded it, in about a week each.

links.took: Turn-based tactical combat; Tim Cain said the team loved X-COM.
links.added: Put that combat inside an open role-playing world with dialogue and moral choices.
links.extra: Cain said Fallout's combat resembled X-COM's before the GURPS license ended.

links.took: An open-ended structure: go anywhere and solve things in any order.
links.added: A post-apocalyptic RPG world where choices change how places and people react.
links.extra: Tim Cain credits Star Control II for the open-ended design of both Fallout and Arcanum.

links.took: The open-ended exploration Tim Cain admired in Star Control II.
links.added: A steam-age fantasy world where magic and technology work against each other.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Control II (cites Tim Cain)

links.took: Fallout's creators, its open-ended quests and its skill-based character building.
links.added: A world in an industrial revolution, with magic and tech aptitudes that cancel each other out.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fallout (Tim Cain called Fallout a 'stepping stone' to Arcanum)

links.extra: Troika Games was founded by Fallout's Tim Cain, Leonard Boyarsky and Jason D. Anderson.

links.took: Troika's turn-based, isometric RPG design.
links.added: A close adaptation of a classic D&D adventure using the 3.5 rules.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Temple of Elemental Evil (video game)

links.took: The 1985 module The Temple of Elemental Evil by Gary Gygax and Frank Mentzer.
links.added: Turn-based tactical combat under the D&D 3.5 rules, a first for a computer game.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Temple of Elemental Evil (video game)

links.took: Fallout creators Tim Cain, Leonard Boyarsky and Jason Anderson, and their reactive quest design.
links.added: A first-person vampire RPG in Los Angeles where your clan changes how you play.
links.extra: The three co-founded Troika Games, which made Bloodlines.

links.took: Valve's Source engine, used while still unfinished, for its facial animation and lip-sync.
links.added: Used the engine for a dialogue-heavy RPG rather than a shooter.
links.extra: Valve's contract barred Bloodlines from launching before Half-Life 2, so both arrived in November 2004.

links.took: White Wolf's vampire clans, disciplines and the Masquerade rule of hiding from humans.
links.added: Fewer abilities for real-time play, and nights in Santa Monica, Hollywood and Chinatown.

links.took: Deus Ex-style first-person role-playing where you can sneak, talk or fight.
links.added: Vampire clans and Los Angeles nightlife instead of a cyberpunk conspiracy.

src.t: Wikipedia: Bloodlines (Eurogamer called it 'Deus Ex with vampires')

links.took: The immersive first-person RPG approach that Ultima Underworld began.
links.added: A modern city setting, vampire powers and dialogue shaped by your clan.

src.t: Wikipedia: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss

links.extra: Wikipedia's Ultima Underworld article lists Bloodlines among the games it influenced.

links.took: The World of Darkness, vampire clans and first-person supernatural powers.
links.added: Moves the story to Seattle; development passed from Hardsuit Labs to The Chinese Room.

links.took: Fallout creators Tim Cain and Leonard Boyarsky, and its darkly comic retro-future tone.
links.added: A corporate-run space colony instead of a nuclear wasteland.

links.took: Obsidian's reactive first-person RPG design, faction reputation and companions.
links.added: Moved the formula into space, with satire aimed at corporations.

links.took: The isometric post-apocalyptic RPG style that Fallout made popular.
links.added: Squad-based turn-based combat and a return to Wasteland's Desert Rangers.
links.extra: Wikipedia's Fallout article lists Wasteland 2 among games Fallout influenced.

links.took: The Desert Rangers, the Arizona setting and several original designers.
links.added: Crowdfunded on Kickstarter and made by Brian Fargo's inXile, 26 years after the first game.

links.took: The Desert Rangers squad and turn-based tactical combat.
links.added: Snowbound Colorado, a drivable armored vehicle and two-player co-op.

links.took: Fallout 2's branching dialogue; Chris Avellone wrote for it while starting Torment.
links.added: A story told almost entirely through conversation, where talking solves most problems.
links.extra: Avellone said Fallout 2 helped him rethink what dialogue could do in Torment.

links.took: Not specified; the game's own credits list Final Fantasy VII as an inspiration.
links.added: Not specified in the source.

links.took: Named by Chris Avellone among the books, comics and games that inspired it.
links.added: Not specified in the source.
links.extra: Avellone said 'Shadowrun' without making clear whether he meant the tabletop game or a video game.

links.took: A modified version of BioWare's Infinity Engine, AD&D rules and a pausable real-time party.
links.added: Sigil, a strange city between planes, and a story about death and identity.

links.took: The Infinity Engine and Baldur's Gate's AD&D party play.
links.added: A focus on combat against large groups in a frozen dungeon crawl.

links.took: The design idea of offering more than one way to reach each goal.
links.added: Real-time combat you can pause, AD&D rules and companions with their own agendas.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls Wasteland a major influence on Baldur's Gate but names no developer.

links.took: Licensed AD&D 2nd edition rules and the Forgotten Realms setting.
links.added: Real-time combat with pause, shown on BioWare's new Infinity Engine.
links.extra: An official AD&D game; its lead programmer read the Forgotten Realms novels to learn the setting.

links.took: BioWare's experience making D&D games with Baldur's Gate.
links.added: Full 3D, D&D 3rd edition rules and a toolset for player-made adventures.

links.took: Its name, and the idea of D&D adventures hosted online for many players.
links.added: A single-player campaign plus player-run servers with a Dungeon Master client.
links.extra: Wikipedia says BioWare's game was named after the 1991 AOL game, the first graphical MMORPG.

links.took: The D&D 3rd edition rule set and the Forgotten Realms city of Neverwinter.
links.added: Tools that let players act as Dungeon Masters for each other online.

links.took: The Forgotten Realms setting, D&D rules and a module-building toolset.
links.added: Obsidian's updated engine, a party of companions and D&D 3.5 rules.

links.took: BioWare's Aurora engine, modified into what became the Odyssey engine.
links.added: Star Wars, a cinematic camera and a light-and-dark-side morality meter.

links.took: Rules from a Star Wars d20 tabletop game built on D&D's third edition.
links.added: Hid the dice rolls behind combat that plays out in real time and can be paused.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

links.took: KOTOR's Odyssey engine, combat system and Old Republic era.
links.added: A darker story that questions the Force itself, led by Chris Avellone at Obsidian.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords

links.took: Lead designer Chris Avellone, who said Torment's Ravel informed the mentor Kreia.
links.added: A morally gray Star Wars story about the cost of the Force.

links.took: KOTOR's morality system, menu-based dialogue and interface.
links.added: Real-time martial arts combat in a world drawn from Chinese myth and wuxia films.

links.took: BioWare's cinematic party RPG; Casey Hudson wanted to evolve KOTOR's pseudo-turn-based combat.
links.added: Real-time third-person shooting, a dialogue wheel and an original sci-fi universe.
links.extra: Drew Karpyshyn, a senior writer on KOTOR, became Mass Effect's lead writer.

links.took: A galaxy with deep alien history; it inspired Mass Effect's writing and character design.
links.added: Cinematic conversations and a squad you lead through a space opera.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Control II (BioWare founder Ray Muzyka cited Star Control)

links.took: Free exploration of star systems and landing on planets in a vehicle.
links.added: Optional uncharted worlds explored in the Mako rover between story missions.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Starflight and Star Control were cited as major inspirations for galaxy exploration and the Mako.

links.took: Party-based tactical fantasy; lead designer Mike Laidlaw called Baldur's Gate its closest comparison.
links.added: An original dark fantasy world, playable origin stories and companions who judge your choices.
links.extra: BioWare often called it a spiritual successor to Baldur's Gate.

links.took: The 'Baldur's Gate roots' that writer David Gaider said the team was returning to.
links.added: A more traditional tactical RPG than Mass Effect, with its own world and rules.
links.extra: Gaider spoke of the series as a whole, not Baldur's Gate II alone.

links.took: BioWare's D&D-style party design; Laidlaw named Neverwinter Nights alongside Baldur's Gate.
links.added: Its own rules system, free of the D&D license.

links.took: Exploration and companions in the style of Baldur's Gate, as Obsidian's pitch put it.
links.added: An original world, Eora, built around souls and reincarnation, with its own rules.

src.t: Obsidian, Project Eternity Kickstarter, via Game Informer, Sep 2012

links.extra: Obsidian pitched it as paying homage to Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dale and Planescape: Torment.

links.took: Icewind Dale's tactical combat and dungeon delving, named in the Kickstarter pitch.
links.added: Directed by Josh Sawyer, an Icewind Dale designer, with a new ruleset.

src.t: Obsidian, Project Eternity Kickstarter, via Game Informer, Sep 2012

links.took: Torment's emotional writing and mature themes, as named in the Kickstarter pitch.
links.added: A story about souls, faith and rebirth in an original setting.

links.took: The Watcher, the world of Eora and pausable real-time party combat.
links.added: A ship to sail between islands, and later an optional turn-based mode.

src.t: Wikipedia: Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire

links.took: Pillars of Eternity's Unity-based engine and gameplay systems.
links.added: A world where evil has already won and you enforce an overlord's law.

links.took: The world of Eora, its gods and its soul-based lore.
links.added: First-person real-time combat and exploration in a region called the Living Lands.

links.took: First-person fantasy exploration with swords and spells.
links.added: Separate hand-built regions instead of one seamless world, plus Obsidian-style companions and dialogue.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

links.extra: Bloomberg reported Obsidian first pitched it as Destiny mixed with Skyrim; Skyrim's article lists Avowed among games it influenced.

links.took: Destiny's shared-world action, part of Obsidian's early pitch, according to Bloomberg.
links.added: Was rebuilt as a single-player RPG set in the Pillars of Eternity world.
links.extra: Director Carrie Patel's overhaul moved the game into the Pillars of Eternity setting.

links.took: Torment's focus on story, ideas and talking your way through problems.
links.added: Monte Cook's Numenera setting and 'Tides' that track how others see you.

src.t: inXile, Kickstarter launch, via PC Gamer, Mar 2013

links.extra: inXile called it a 'thematic successor'; Colin McComb, a Planescape: Torment designer, led its creative work.

links.took: The Ninth World setting and Monte Cook's Numenera rules.
links.added: A story-heavy isometric RPG built on that tabletop world.

links.took: A grounded view of late-medieval German life, faith and superstition.
links.added: A choice-driven mystery in 16th-century Bavaria, drawn like a manuscript.

src.t: Wikipedia: Darklands (IGN called it a direct inspiration for Pentiment)

links.took: Director Josh Sawyer, who also directed Pillars of Eternity.
links.added: A narrative mystery with no combat, built around history and conversation.

links.took: The Shadowrun world of magic and cyberware, and its co-creator Jordan Weisman.
links.added: A turn-based tactics RPG funded on Kickstarter, with an editor for fan campaigns.

links.took: Mass Effect's squad combat, alien species and conversation choices.
links.added: A new galaxy, planets to settle and a jump-jet for faster combat.

links.took: Thedas, returning companions and the Dread Wolf plot set up in Inquisition.
links.added: Fast real-time action combat and a new protagonist called Rook.

links.took: Skyrim's success with very large open-world fantasy RPGs.
links.added: Wide open regions to explore, held together by BioWare's party and story focus.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

links.extra: Wikipedia credits Skyrim with popularizing large fantasy open worlds and influencing The Witcher and Dragon Age.
